text:
Evidence supports testing objectives before changing NextItNet’s backbone. *On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax Loss for Item Recommendation* (2024) shows that sampled softmax emphasizes hard negatives and connects optimization to DCG; temperature controls hardness, with overly aggressive settings letting a few negatives dominate. Its experiments concern collaborative filtering, so transfer to NextItNet remains a hypothesis. [Paper](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf). *Improved Estimation of Ranks* (2024) develops sampled WARP/LambdaRank with corrected rank estimates, demonstrating that sampling bias can undermine ranking objectives. [Paper summary](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/).

Importance correction needs care. *Correcting the LogQ Correction* (RecSys 2025) identifies a flaw in conventional correction: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its refined derivation accounts for that distinction and improves retrieval results. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331). Hardness also does not establish negative-label reliability: *UFNRec* (2023) specifically studies false negatives in sequential recommendation. [Paper](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/1.9781611977653.ch6).

Practical experiment proposal: preserve one NextItNet scoring head and compare baseline training against multi-negative sampled softmax; then vary temperature, negative count, and uniform versus stochastic mixed sampling. Exclude known training positives from negatives. Apply importance correction using the actual sampling probabilities; deterministic top-score mining cannot simply inherit uniform-sampling correction. Treat moderate hardness and warm-up as hypotheses, not established improvements. Select solely by the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10: catalog-ranking theory and published gains do not guarantee improvement against 99 sampled negatives. All changes remain training objectives or samplers within one independently trained model per category.
